record.paper_title: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism. Maxent-Nesom: Concepts, Construction, Application, Open Questions and Criticisms
record.context_brief: choice of constraints and relevant variables
record.original_question: In a MaxEnt-NESOM description of a nonequilibrium many-body system, how should one determine the available-information constraints: specifically, the basic dynamical variables, independent internal thermodynamic parameters, and macroscopic observables appropriate to the system and experiment, given Bogoliubov's hierarchy of relaxation times and the requirement that the description use quasi-conserved variables rather than arbitrary constraints?

evidence.quote: Consequently, the first fundamental step in the present situation is to decide on the basic set of dynamical variables appropriate for the description of the macroscopic state of the nonequilibrium system.

L. L Buishvili and M. D. Zviadadze discuss the problem of the choice of the independent internal thermodynamic parameters for the description of nonequilibrium systems on the basis of Bogoliubov's idea concerning the hierarchy of relaxation times as well as successive reductions in the description of nonequilibrium states of the system when it tends to equilibrium.
MaxEnt is likely to be sound, but often it is dreadfully difficult to understand what the constraints are.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a many-body system out of equilibrium, to be described within the Maximum-Entropy Nonequilibrium Statistical Operator Method (MaxEnt-NESOM). In this framework, a statistical operator is constructed by maximizing the Gibbs–Shannon entropy subject to a set of constraints of the form Tr{ρ(t) P_j} = Q_j(t), where {P_j} is a chosen basis of dynamical (microscopic) operators and {Q_j(t)} are the corresponding macrovariables that characterize the nonequilibrium macroscopic state. Assume Bogoliubov's principle of a hierarchy of relaxation times, namely that the time evolution of the system separates into successive stages in which progressively fewer, longer-lived (quasi-conserved) collective variables suffice to describe the macroscopic state as the system relaxes towards equilibrium.

Provide a general, constructive criterion that, for a given nonequilibrium many-body system and a given experimental probing scale (time resolution and observed macroscopic observables), determines:

(i) the basic set of microscopic dynamical variables {P_j} that must enter the constraints;
(ii) the corresponding independent internal thermodynamic parameters (Lagrange multipliers) {F_j(t)} conjugate to {Q_j(t)}; and
(iii) the set of macroscopic observables appropriate to the description,

such that the chosen variables are quasi-conserved on the relevant timescale (as opposed to arbitrary constraints), and such that the resulting truncated description is closed, self-consistent, and reproduces the observed macroscopic dynamics. Establish the criterion explicitly and prove that it yields a unique minimal sufficient set of constraints for each level of the Bogoliubov hierarchy.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how to systematically select the basic set of dynamical variables and constraints in MaxEnt-NESOM remains an acknowledged open foundational issue in nonequilibrium statistical mechanics. Subsequent reviews of the formalism (by Luzzi, Vasconcellos, Ramos and collaborators) continue to treat the choice of basic variables as guided by physical insight and Bogoliubov's hierarchy of relaxation times rather than by a universal algorithmic criterion. No general theorem providing a unique constructive rule appears to be established.

status_evidence.title: Predictive Statistical Mechanics: A Nonequilibrium Statistical Ensemble Formalism
status_evidence.snippet: The choice of basic dynamical variables is left to physical considerations based on Bogoliubov's hierarchy of relaxation times.
status_evidence.claim: Reference works on MaxEnt-NESOM still treat the selection of constraints as a physically guided, not algorithmically determined, step.
